claims.confidence: high for policy direction; medium for Polish monetization
claims.statement: A future fleet of SME batteries and flexible loads needs aggregation because EU market design explicitly promotes storage, demand response, energy sharing and active customer participation; measurable value is lower bills and market flexibility revenue.
The prospective business could seek dispatch rights through capacity-reservation contracts, but no devices, contracts, metering access or market authorization are currently controlled.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: SME owner or energy manager; aggregator partnership economics unknown
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Vendor-neutral pooling across battery brands and installers; utilities and battery vendors can bundle dispatch
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future co-ownership boundaries with an aggregator must be contractually defined
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Solar installers, battery installers and energy consultants

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 1,000-3,000 PLN per enrolled site via installer channels
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Assumption: monthly settlement after aggregator or supplier pays; settlement lag unknown
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 35-60% of service revenue after aggregator and telemetry costs
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Device integration, exception handling and customer support; unknown by hardware mix
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Energy-law counsel, cybersecurity, insurance and metering certification
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Share of verified savings/flexibility revenue plus platform fee
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Gateway hardware, API fees, aggregator share and field service

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Utilities, aggregators and battery OEMs can bundle optimization into supply or hardware contracts
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Monthly verified bill savings or flexibility payment generated by dispatchable batteries and loads
commercial_mechanics.payer: Participating SME from savings, or licensed aggregator from market revenue
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Battery installation, dynamic tariff adoption or painful demand charges
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual capacity reservation and continuing monthly settlement

contrary_evidence: Polish market-access rules and available revenue stacks may not support small portfolios.
Hardware fragmentation and customer overrides can destroy dispatch reliability.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: No current instrument; proposed capacity-reservation contracts with SMEs plus an aggregator agreement
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Offer bill analytics without dispatch or recruit capacity through a different aggregator
critical_control_point.current_owner: SMEs own devices; suppliers, DSOs and licensed market actors control key data and settlement rails
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future co-ownership boundaries with an aggregator must be contractually defined
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Consent-based installer relationships may be explored; no family-company customers or device data are assumed
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business jointly with signed device owners and a licensed market-access partner
critical_control_point.subject: Dispatch rights over a pooled SME battery and flexible-load fleet

economics.acquisition_route: Start with simulation and bill audit, secure one aggregator sandbox, then contract 20-50 compatible sites
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 1,500 sites producing 2,400 PLN annual net revenue each yields 3.6m PLN revenue; at 25% EBITDA and a 6-8x value, founder equity could exceed 5m PLN in years 7-10. Revenue per site and regulatory access are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly until integrations and operations are hired
economics.gross_margin_basis: Platform and performance revenue less settlement partner, telemetry and field support
economics.payback: Assumption: 24-36 months because integration precedes portfolio density
economics.pricing: Assumption: 20-30% of verified value plus 50-150 PLN monthly per site
economics.retention_or_repeat: Multi-year device life and recurring monthly dispatch

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Dispatch-response history and a dense pool of compatible SME capacity
fingerprint.customer: SMEs with batteries, EV charging or controllable loads
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Flexibility pooling and optimization on revenue share
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: SME or aggregator pays when verified savings or flexibility revenue settles
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Distributed assets proliferate but remain too small and fragmented to monetize

founder_fit: Renewable-energy family context can inform integrations with consent.
Capital fits a narrow software-first pilot, not asset ownership.

structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: licensed polish market access and settlement

structure.critical_dependency: Licensed market-access partner and compatible metering

thesis: Future state: thousands of Polish SMEs own flexible batteries and loads but cannot individually monetize them. The missing contractual and coordination mechanism is a dispatchable pool with verified baselines, customer permissions and market settlement.
title: SME Battery-Flexibility Pool
